facts.text: South Brunswick takes its name from New Brunswick, which itself was named after the German city of Braunschweig, once a powerful Hanseatic League member.
South Brunswick Township was officially incorporated by the New Jersey Legislature in 1798, marking the start of its formal governance.
Attorney Dayton helped settle disputes over the Freehold and Jamesburg Agricultural Railroad's right‑of‑way, shaping early transportation routes.
The South Brunswick Local History Blog offers a curated collection of posts detailing the township’s past, from early settlers to modern milestones.
The Pigeon Swamp Ledger, dating back to the 1780s, records laws, accounts, and memoranda from early South Brunswick residents.
